summary: Suspended autopay after private key rotation caused duplicate warmup credit and invoice hold
description: Issue summary: BrightShelf reported a billing hold and autopay suspension on 2026-03-12 after a scheduled private key rotation for their BrightShelf private deployment in eu-west-1. The account shows two anomalous behaviors: (1) a duplicate warmup credit line was applied and later reversed on the provisional invoice, and (2) an automated fraud/reconciliation workflow placed the account on autopay hold pending manual review, causing invoice autopay to fail and triggering collection alerts. Impact: customer-facing invoices are on hold, autopay disabled, and BrightShelf cannot complete the monthly payment. Business impact: potential customer churn and manual payments required for a large enterprise account. Environment: BrightShelf private deployment (VPC) in eu-west-1; private control plane with customer-managed keys; new key rotated at 2026-03-12T02:05:08Z.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Rotate private deployment API key following the runbook (simulate the same key ID swap and proxy edge rollout).
2) Send concurrent warmup/postback events from edge proxies with the old key id and new key id during overlapping rollout window.
3) Trigger reconciler postback ingestion with retry window enabled (simulate transient 500s for primary ingest to force retries).
4) Observe postback dedupe fingerprinting and subsequent credit application logic.
5) Check billing reconciler actions and autopay/fraud flags set by the billing rules engine.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: support confirmed BrightShelf saw provisional invoice lines with two warmup credit lines of identical amount and fingerprint, followed by a reversal for one line in the subsequent reconciliation window.

Hypothesis 1: overlapping key rotation caused identical postbacks to be ingested as separate events because dedupe uses (fingerprint, key_id) instead of (fingerprint) across key swaps. This led to two warmup credits being applied in different provisional invoices before dedupe/reconciliation kicked in.

Hypothesis 2: billing fraud/reconciliation automation treats rapid duplicate credits from different key_ids as potential test/proxy traffic and triggers an autopay_hold for manual review. The rule thresholds are conservative for enterprise private deployments and were hit by BrightShelf's concurrent rollout.

Data pulled: reconciler ingestion traces (traces/ingest/2026-03-12/bright-123), billing event table queries showed two credit insert events with identical postback_fp=fp_9b2a at 02:05:14 and 02:05:40 assigned to prov-7899 and prov-7900.

Temporary artifacts: reconciler backlog shows retried messages with old key id that were processed after messages with new key id; dedupe code path treated them as unique because key_id is part of dedupe key.

SRE note: we reproduced locally by simulating a 5-10s window where proxies report both old and new key ids; reconciler double-applies credits when the dedupe window is misaligned with the rotation event.
Relevant dashboards: Billing > Credits > Warmup > By fingerprint (tile), Reconciler > Postback Duplication Rate, Fraud > Autopay Holds by trigger

resolution_notes: Action items and temporary resolution: 1) Finance Ops prepared an invoice-level manual adjustment to remove the duplicate warmup credit and re-assign the single expected credit to the active provisional invoice; adjustment scheduled 2026-03-14T18:00 UTC. 2) Support cleared the autopay_hold after Finance applied the adjustment and confirmed with BrightShelf to re-enable autopay. 3) Engineering implemented a short-term reconciler patch to dedupe postbacks by fingerprint alone for events within a 60s rotation window (PR referenced). 4) Long-term: add explicit rotation marker in postback payloads and a reconciler feature to collapse identical fingerprints across key_id changes; add telemetry dashboards and an ops runbook addendum for private key rotations. Follow-ups: monitor for reoccurrence for 7 days; Finance to issue confirmation and credit memos if any finalized invoices were affected.
